newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar/yen surge.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar/yen surge.

text.p: The South Korean won plunged to its lowest level in almost seven years against the U.S. dollar on Friday as the dollar's surge in Tokyo put further pressure on the local currency, dealers said.
It closed at 854.60 after opening at 853.30 and hitting an 83-month low of 856.00 in intra-day trading before the central bank intervened by selling dollars.
The Bank of Korea denied intervening.
In Tokyo, the dollar rose to 120 yen, its highest point since February 1993.
Dealers said the won was expected to remain weak as dollar demand for importer settlements outweighed supply.
"What matters is only the speed and the won's weakness will continue for a considerable period," said on bank dealer.
"There are few tools available to stop the dollar's rise. I see this pace continuing at least during the first quarter," said Ha Jong-soo, a Korea Exchange Bank dealer.
Dealers saw the won's base mid-rate for Monday at around 854.10, the same as on Friday.
